prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1376; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported today that a sideswipe occurred while the insured was changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the insured is listed as a named driver on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the reported loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report. It records the collision, identifies the claimant as present in the vehicle, and notes two witnesses who stopped at the scene.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who described the lane change and the contact between the two vehicles in terms that match the insured's account of the event.

Entry 5: Reviewed the scene photographs. The damage to the insured's vehicle lines up with the side impact described by the parties and the witnesses.

Entry 6: Interviewed the first witness, who confirmed seeing the sideswipe and the vehicles separating afterward. The witness also confirmed that the claimant was seated in the passenger area.

Entry 7: Received the claimant's injury description through counsel, which reports a back strain. The kind and force of the impact appear consistent with that injury.

Entry 8: Received the initial treatment records. The care began promptly after the accident and followed a typical course for this type of soft tissue injury.

Entry 9: During a second recorded conversation, the claimant described the direction of the impact differently than in the first call. The claimant also gave a different count of the occupants in the car.

Entry 10: A neighbor contacted the desk and stated that the vehicle appeared to already be damaged some weeks before the reported loss. No photographs or other records have been provided to support this.

Entry 11: Checked prior claims and loss databases. No earlier injury to the same area of the body and no earlier damage to the insured vehicle appear in the records.

Entry 12: Treatment has tapered as the claimant's symptoms improved, and the file is being held pending counsel's response to the discrepancies in the claimant's recorded statements and the neighbor's information.
